History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old female with 3-day history of worsening right-sided, photophobia-associated headache consistent with probable migraine; advised stronger analgesia, headache diary, and follow-up in 1–2 weeks.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Headache.  
• Onset: Began ~3 days ago while at work.  
• Course/progression: Constant baseline pain with intermittent surges; overall worsening each day.  
• Location: Generalized but predominant around the right eye.  
• Character: Dull baseline, occasionally sharp; gradual onset.  
• Severity: 8/10.  
• Exacerbating factors: Bright light; computer work; possible stress.  
• Relieving factors attempted: Ibuprofen 3 tablets/day for 2 days—minimal relief; reduced screen brightness—some help.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia (“hurts to look at bright lights”), episodic “shooting lights,” nausea without vomiting, difficulty focusing.  
• Pertinent negatives: No vision loss or persistent blurring, no neck stiffness, no speech difficulty, no limb weakness, no recent head trauma, no fever, no rash.  
• First episode of this intensity; prior ordinary headaches usually resolved with ibuprofen.  

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No personal history of migraine.  
• No regular medications.  
• Glasses for vision correction since age 5.  

Social History:
• Lives with three housemates.  
• Occupation: IT; prolonged screen time.  
• Tobacco: Social smoker.  
• Alcohol: Social drinker.  
• Reports mild work stress due to new project.  

Family History:
• Mother: Recurrent, season-triggered migraines, occasionally disabling.  
• Sister: Infrequent migraines.  
• No other familial conditions mentioned.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• General/neuro/HEENT examinations: Not performed (tele-consult).

Investigations:
• None ordered or reviewed during visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Probable migraine-type headache  
  • Plan:  
    – Optimize NSAID dosing: Ibuprofen up to 400 mg (two tablets) three times daily with food.  
    – Provide prescription for alternative NSAID (Naproxen) and consider adjunct analgesics (Paracetamol or Codeine; dose/route/frequency not documented).  
    – Initiate headache diary to record frequency, severity, and potential triggers.  
    – Recommend eye examination if ongoing visual strain.  
    – Safety-net advice: Return sooner for worsening pain, visual changes, neurological deficits, or concern.  
    – Follow-up: Review in 1–2 weeks; discuss prophylactic therapy if headaches become frequent.

General plan items  
  • Encourage adequate hydration, regular meals, stress management.  
  • Continue social smoking/alcohol discussion at future visits as needed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Vitals, focused neurological and HEENT examination, detailed medication reconciliation (patient not asked about OTC, supplements), oral contraceptive use status.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
